lines.watchItem: Cloud and accelerator buyers keep raising 2026 spending plans, and the wafer makers behind them now run their lines flat out with 300mm prices starting to rise. Leading-edge wafer demand is exposed to how long that spending pace and the wafer squeeze both hold.

Advanced-packaging lines stay booked through 2027 at 52 to 78 week waits, while the shortfall narrows from about 20 percent to roughly 10 percent as monthly capacity climbs toward 130,000 wafers. How fast that gap closes sets how much of the order book converts into shipped revenue.

Memory is now the tighter limit than packaging: one supplier says it can cover only about half of what customers ask for, and NVIDIA has cut memory per accelerator on its next flagship to raise unit output. Packaging slots freed up by smaller memory stacks are exposed to whether memory relief actually arrives.

Three customers hold more than 85 percent of advanced-packaging capacity, with NVIDIA alone reserving roughly 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of the 2026 total. That concentration means one buyer's order change moves a large block of capacity at once.

Custom hyperscaler chips are growing far faster than merchant GPUs, Microsoft is negotiating capacity for upward of 300,000 of its own accelerators for 2027, and MediaTek has lifted its share target. The leading-node customer base is shifting from a few merchant vendors toward a wider set of custom-chip programs.

AMD's data-center sales more than doubled to $6.7 billion and its racks are in production, yet it reports only $222 million of contracted obligations beyond a year and splits about a tenth of packaging capacity between its processors and accelerators. Its announced gigawatt deals turning into booked wafer demand is the open question.

Pricing holds firm across the chain: TSMC posted a 67.7 percent gross margin and lifted full-year growth guidance above 40 percent, NVIDIA held 75 percent, and memory suppliers are pushing contract prices up by double digits. Pricing power tracks how long that shortage-driven firmness lasts and how much of it memory makers absorb.

Intel foundry revenue rose 31 percent to $5.8 billion, its bridge packaging is winning a multi-million-unit Google order at a reported cost well below CoWoS, and NVIDIA is weighing moving some output there. A credible second packaging route is forming, though its silicon-capacitor supplier is already fully booked and the technology suits custom chips better than high-bandwidth accelerators.
